text:
alex: Heads-up — p99 latency jumped ~2.3x in prod right after the v3.1 rollout at 09:12 UTC. Canary looked fine. Anyone seeing this?
ops-bot: deploy: model:v3.1 -> rollout started by @maria at 2026-03-17T09:11:58Z, batch=canary->50%->100%

maria: I see the spike on the per-route dashboard. p50 ~140ms -> 230ms, p99 ~480ms -> 1.15s. RPS stable. GPU util nudged up but not saturated. Quick snippet from Grafana:
```
route: text-gen/default
window: 5m
req/s: 420 -> 410
p50: 140ms -> 230ms
p95: 260ms -> 540ms
p99: 480ms -> 1150ms
gpu_util: 62% -> 76%
```

raj: pulled a perf profile from the affected host. Kernel selection log looks noisy — a bunch of layers are falling back to fp32 kernels even though quantization metadata exists. Example:
```
[kernel_selector] layer=17 expected=int8_matmul selected=fp32_gemm reason=quant_meta_mismatch
[kernel_selector] layer=18 expected=int8_matmul selected=fp32_gemm reason=sequence_len_gt_threshold
[batcher] input_seq_len=124 avg_seq_len=118 batch_size=4 -> using conservative path
```

chen: fwiw tokenizer changes in v3.1 include a new merge rule (subword-split fix). That raised avg tokens per request in our sample by ~1.8x. KV cache memory per request increased accordingly. I dumped eviction counters:
```
kv_cache_evictions_total: increased 0 -> 84/min after rollout
kv_cache_hits: down 98.4% -> 89.1%
```

samantha: Putting two things together: tokenizer -> longer sequences -> higher KV pressure + more layers hitting >seq-len threshold -> kernel selector chooses safe/fallback kernels that are slower. Also batching heuristics might be shrinking effective batch sizes (more variance in seq lengths), so throughput per-GPU drops and latency climbs.

alex: That matches what I'm seeing in traces — many requests show a long gap during KV restore/evict. Any quick mitigation we can do?

maria: Short-term: rollback v3.1 to v3.0 for the problematic pool (dedicated + high-traffic routes). I'll start rollback for the shared prod pool now.
ops-bot: rollback: model:v3.1 -> model:v3.0 initiated by @maria at 2026-03-17T09:25:18Z

raj: Medium-term: patch kernel_selector to be sequence-length-aware in the other direction — if quant_meta exists but seq len slightly > threshold, prefer quant kernel with fallback to autopromote paths rather than switching to full fp32 for entire layer. I can prototype a heuristic: if avg_seq_len < threshold * 1.3 and gpu_memory_headroom>10% then allow int8 path.

chen: Also we should tune KV cache sizing / eviction policy for sudden seq-length increases: right now we use strict LRU with a small per-worker cap. Maybe switch to segmented LRU or increase per-worker KV budget for 24h after rollouts.

maria: Repro steps to validate locally (use this load generator):
```
# reproduce with v3.1 tokenizer + real seq distribution
python tools/load_test.py --model v3.1 --seq-dist samples/v3.1-seq-hist.json --rps 400 --duration 300
# record kernel chooser debug logs
export REDWOOD_KERNEL_DEBUG=1
```

samantha: I'm going to run a quick A/B run against a staging pool with the modified kernel_selector flags (allow_int8_relaxed=true) and increase kv cache cap by 30% to see effect. Will report numbers in ~15m.

alex: Thanks. Maria — keep rollback in place until we validate fixes. Raj/Chen/Samantha — coordinate on a patch and a controlled canary. Post the perf diffs here.

maria: rollback completed for pool-prod-1, traffic routed to v3.0. p99 already trending down toward baseline. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: traffic_switch: pool-prod-1 now serving model:v3.0 (at 2026-03-17T09:33:05Z)

raj: initial canary with relaxed int8 heuristic on staging: p99 reduced by ~30% relative to strict fallback; int8 kernels executed for ~65% of layers vs 22% before. Kernel trace:
```
layer=17 selected=int8_matmul reason=relaxed_threshold
layer=18 selected=int8_matmul reason=relaxed_threshold
```

chen: staging KV metric after +30% cap: eviction rate dropped to near-zero, kv_hit 97.6%. Latencies look good.

samantha: I'll open a PR with the kernel heuristic + flags, include rollout gating and telemetry we want (kernel_choice sampling, seq_len histograms). PR: https://git.redwood/eng/runtime/pull/4923 (WIP)

alex: Cool. Once PR is green, we'll do a slow canary to prod with rollback plan attached. Add a postmortem note about tokenizer change testing (we need seq-distribution checks in model onboarding). Owners: rollback/maria, kernel_patch/raj, kv_policy/chen, canary/samantha.

maria: filing incident ticket and linking perf artifacts. ticket: INF-2026-1123

alex: Thanks everyone. Keep updates here.
